newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said there were two sorts of Commission meeting minutes; one referring to the Commission's collegial decisions and the other to the Commissioners' remarks. Van der Pas said these minutes were confidential and had not and would not be published.
Van der Pas said all the relevant Commission minutes had been made available for the EP inquiry commitee on BSE but that it had not responded to the invitation.

Referring to reports on this issue, van de Pas said the Commission deplored the selectivity in the choice of the quotes from the minutes and denied any complicity between the Commission and the UK in the BSE crisis.

He said that what mattered for the Commission was to assess past events and prepare better tools to face such complex issues, notably the forthcoming one on genetically modified organisms. The Commission will do so internally by reorganising its services and will propose reorganising the veterinary committee and network to reinforce controls, he said.

Asked about the news magazine Der Spiegel's report that Commissioner Martin Bangemann had accepted 10,000 marks to attend a conference in Switzerland, spokeman Jochen Kubosch said Bangemann had been offered such an amount but denied that it was either accepted or paid.

Asked why the above-mentioned article had been taken out of the Commission's press review between its first and the second copy, van der Pas said this was not an issue to be discussed in the news room but was an internal Commission matter.

In answer to a question, spokeswoman Elisabetta Olivi said the Commission had sent a reasoned opinion to the French authorities because it was convinced that the directive on public procurement contracts had not been fully respected as regards the construction of the "Grand Stade de France" near Paris in preparation of the 1998 soccer World Cup.
Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said Commissioner Hans van den Broek would make an official visit in Prague on Thursday and Friday to discuss the Czech Republic's plans to join the EU.
He also said that the opinions regarding membership would be sent after the conclusion of the inter-governmental conference whenever that was.
Van der Pas said Commissioner Marcelino Oreja's document on reinforced cooperation would be available from 1500/1400 GMT in his office in French, English and German.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/33: Public procurement: Commission sends reasoned opinion to France on World cup stadium.
- IP/97/34: Cohesion and the Information Society.
- IP/97/35: The Commission adopts green paper on vertical restraints in EU competition policy.
- IP/97/36: Commission initiates proceedings against extension of aid scheme in Sicily.
- IP/97/38: Commission decides to open proceedings with regard to aid for Neptun Industrie Rostock and Dieselmotorenwerk Vulkan.
- IP/97/39: Commission approves the release of a final tranche of restructuring aid for the Peene Werft.
- IP/97/40: Commission seeks clarification concerning French horserace betting measures.
- IP/97/41: The Commission clears the acquisition of the British bottler Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages by Coca-Cola Enterprises, Inc.
- IP/97/42: The Commission invites comments on the envisaged revision of the notice on agreements of minor importance ("de Minimis").
- IP/97/43: The Commission opens a procedure against a state aid scheme for combined transport in the Netherlands.
- IP/97/44: Commissioner van den Broek visits the Czech Republic.
- Speech/97/13: Speech by Commissioner Wulf-Mathies on cohesion and the information society.
- Memo/97/6: Enlargement: 30 questions and answers.
- Memo/97/7: EU/Czech Republic relations.
- Oil bulletin No 852.
- Selling prices of petroleum products in Ecus and in US dollars.
- ME97/22.1: Midday Express.
